thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: high rate of GPU prefill OOMs on inference-prod-us-east-1 cluster. 5 container restarts in the last 180s for model gptx-13b-quant. Auto-restart triggered. Paging oncall.

alice: saw the alert, looking now. Which pools?

incident-bot: Affected pods: inference-prod-us-east-1/gptx-13b-quant-*: container_restart_count >= 1, error log contains 'CUDA out of memory' and 'prefill buffer overflow'. Router latency spike at 2026-03-15T14:02:xxZ.

bob: I can tail the logs. Pulling kubectl describe + pod logs.

carol: @alice @bob marking P1. Do we have customer-facing impact yet?

dave: Support seeing a few customers reporting 502s and truncated responses for long-context requests to the hosted API. Ticket #INC-4121 opened, some customers showing multiple failures.

frank: grabbing logs from the runtime agent. snippet from pod log:

```
[2026-03-15T14:01:05Z] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.07 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 27.40 GiB already allocated; 3.85 GiB free; 4.12 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
prefill.cpp: line 211: prefill buffer overflow: requested 524288 tokens > buffer 262144
```

bob: that "prefill buffer overflow" indicates very large context/prefix. Looks like a single request attempted a massive prefill (long prompt + huge system context). Container OOM then k8s restarted it.

alice: immediate mitigations: 1) throttling on router for requests with large content-length headers; 2) add a temporary reject rule for inputs > 500k tokens for gptx-13b-quant; 3) scale up worker pool to absorb in-flight requests while we patch. I'll apply (1) and (2) now.

frank: can we hotpatch runtime to do prefill-size checks before allocating VRAM? That would avoid the OOM and return 413. If quick, we should deploy to prod.

bob: hotpatch is doable but needs a restart of the runtime process on the pool. Risky but likely safe if we roll canary. I can prepare a minimal guard that checks token count and rejects > limit.

carol: while we prepare hotpatch, do rate-limits and router rejects. Also, please cordon the nodes with repeated restarts to prevent noisy restarts and spreading.

alice: implemented router rule: requests where header X-Input-Token-Count > 500000 are returned 413 with body 'input too large for prefill'. Also enabled moderate client-side throttling for streaming prefill paths. Confirmed reduced request volume.

incident-bot: Router rule active. Observed prefill request rate drop by 18% in 3m.

frank: pushing hotfix branch: prefill_size_guard. It adds a pre-check that calculates estimated tokens from utf8 bytes and prompt metadata and rejects at RPC-level before allocation. Running smoke on staging.

bob: staging smoke passed. Canarying to 10% of the gptx-13b-quant pool. Deploying in 2m.

alice: canary looks good, no OOMs during 5m window on canary replicas. Increasing rollout to 50%.

dave: Customer impact update: ~0.8% of overall requests to the hosted API returned 502 during the spike window; for gptx-13b-quant prefill endpoints error rate peaked at ~12%. Two customers (internal redacted orgs) reported degraded user experience. No data loss.

eva: flagging this for product: long-system prompts + large context customers could be affected. We should consider documented soft-limits and SDK client-side guards.

grace: I'm taking the on-call handoff in 20m. Please leave a short summary for next oncall.

alice: summary for handoff: cause = large prefill requests triggered prefill buffer overflow -> CUDA OOM -> container restarts. Immediate mitigations = router rejects for >500k tokens, client throttling on streaming prefill, cordon noisy nodes, canary+rollout of prefill_size_guard to reject oversized requests pre-allocation. Hotfix rolling to 100% at 14:24Z.

bob: actions I'm owning: 1) postmortem with timeline and reproducer; 2) add automated metric + alert for prefills with estimated token > 250k (to catch earlier); 3) review prefill buffer sizing and add graceful allocation fallback.

frank: actions I'm owning: 1) merge hotfix into main and backport to maintenance branch; 2) add unit test for prefill estimation; 3) prepare a config option to drop or stream large prefill in chunks.

carol: ops actions: 1) verify drained nodes healthy and rejoin cluster; 2) update runbook to include router-level reject rule for massive prefills; 3) update incident severity timeline.

dave: support actions: 1) notify impacted customers with summary + mitigation steps (we've queued outgoing messages for two affected accounts); 2) map affected API keys to customers and follow up if they need help adjusting prompts.

alice: rolling to 100% complete at 14:24Z. No further restarts seen in the last 8m. Monitoring for 30m.

incident-bot: Summary posted to incident channel: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/incidents/1905554321, incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

grace: taking the handoff now. Thanks team. I'll own the 4-hour watch and follow the postmortem. Make sure the reproducer and logs are uploaded to the ticket.

alice: uploaded logs and reproducer script to the incident ticket. Reproducer: sends a simulated prefill with 600k tokens built from repeated long system messages. Use cautiously (will trigger OOM on unpatched nodes).

frank: note for postmortem: add recommendation to add SDK-level fast-fail for extremely large prompts and documentation for model-specific max context guidance.

carol: leaving this thread open for the handoff. If anything else spikes, react with :rotating_light: and we'll re-escalate.

grace: acknowledged. Closing active paging. We'll schedule the postmortem and list follow-ups in a follow-up thread.

alice: final note: no PII exposed, no persisted state corruption. Root cause: missing guard on prefill allocation for oversized inputs combined with router allowing very large bodies.

incident-bot: Incident ticket updated: status=monitoring, severity=P2 (customer-affecting but mitigated), assignees=[bob, frank, carol, dave], timeline attached.
